cite_runs: [Reporter @ Loudoun Times]. “Wary of Lawsuits, Loudoun Supervisors Seek Legal Analysis of Ending Data Center Grandfathering.” Loudoun Times-Mirror, 2 Sept. 20
body: An attempt by two Loudoun County supervisors to change a rule around data center applications is on pause as the Board of Supervisors seeks a legal opinion. ⁋ Supervisors Juli Briskman, D-Algonkian, and Laura TeKrony, D-Little River, brought an initiative to a Sept. 1 board meeting that would kick-start
a resolution that could end data center "grandfathering" in the county.

⁋ The push comes 18 months after the board voted in 2025 to end all by-right data center development in the county, requiring all applications to come before the board for an exception to the zoning ordinance. ⁋ That decision allowed by-right applications already in the pipeline to continue without needing a board vote. Supervisors voted 5-4 to allow grandfathering, with Supervisors Mike Turner, D-Ashburn; Sylvia Glass, D-Broad Run; TeKrony; and Briskman opposed. ⁋ That means 25 applications are currently “grandfathered in” and don’t need board approval, according to the county. ⁋ Briskman and TeKrony want to change that, and take those data centers through a public process and board vote instead. ⁋ TeKrony said ending grandfathering would “give citizens their voice” and protect public health, safety, and quality of life. ⁋ “Residents deserve a voice in what is built next to their home, schools, and parks. Loudoun is oversaturated with data centers,” she said. “Residents are telling us, ‘enough is enough.’ Why should Loudoun have to shoulder the burden of all the data centers to serve the world?” ⁋ Loudoun had 209 completed data centers and 43 under construction at the start of this year, according to the county commissioner of the revenue. ⁋ While the original motion would have brought a resolution ending grandfathering to an October vote, that’s not what the board passed. Instead, supervisors voted unanimously to study whether it’s legal to end grandfathering. ⁋ County Attorney Leo Rogers is expected to return to the board Oct. 6 with his legal opinion. The staff will also bring an inventory of the grandfathered data center applications. ⁋
Briskman and TeKrony said the board needed to stop data center development in response to intense community backlash.

She asked the board to end grandfathering. ⁋ “Our community is not opposed to growth or responsible development. We support development that is compatible with and respectful of the surrounding environment and existing neighborhoods. What we oppose is the placement of industrial-scale data centers immediately adjacent to residential communities." ⁋ Jurgens lives near George Washington University’s Virginia Science and Technology Campus in Ashburn and is organizing community resistance to Amazon data centers planned for the site. ⁋ Other speakers were against ending grandfathering, including union representatives. ⁋ “I live in Northern Virginia, and I’m here because these projects are very important to our members’ livelihoods. What you decide tonight is going to reach well beyond you in this room. If that analysis confirms the Board has the authority to act, we should be prepared to act swiftly.”
